background.speaker: SPEAKER_01
background.text: I want to talk about housing specifically. I mean, they would need to drop 32% to be as affordable as they were in 2015. You acknowledged rent costs are up as well. How do you help the families who are at the bottom end, who are facing rental increases, who can hardly afford a small place to live, up to the middle ground people who would have been able to afford a house seven years ago, and now they can't. And possibly won't be able to if they stay where they are at a $600,000 average cost of a home here. What do you say to that?

background.speaker: [target]
background.text: Yeah, I shared that, that just came out a few days ago, that study, really well done, and you guys covered it, and I sent it to all my senior staff, because this is the challenge we face. I mean, essentially,

background.speaker: [target]
background.text: We don't have the numbers, but we basically went from about $400,000 to about $600,000 for an average house in the metro area, roughly speaking. And obviously, there's areas in our state where it's more expensive than that. That is coupled with higher interest rates on mortgages. So people's buying power is less. Home prices, they've probably stabilized. They've only gone up in the last few months. Maybe they even go down a little bit, but still, effectively, they're going up because your mortgage rate is up if you're getting into a new mortgage. So what we need to do is we need to get some of the onerous requirements that suppress the quantity of housing out of the way to have more housing close to where jobs are. And also, again, not just any housing. We need housing in the threes and the fours, 300s, 400s. That's what we need, right? I mean, there's always going to be demand for people buying million-dollar homes and a few here and there. But what we really need are the 300s and 400s. And then we also need affordable access to rental for people that are an important part of our workforce. We hope they aspire to homeowners. We hope they aspire to homeownership someday. But while you're saving up that down payment, you might be in a rental for a while, and we need to make sure that that's also close to where you live. We all benefit because it also means less traffic on our roads and better air quality if we can pull this off.

background.speaker: SPEAKER_01
background.text: Where do we build these $300,000, $400,000 houses and how do we build them?

ground_truth: Yeah. So what it means is, again, two things. It's on transit corridors. So this is areas where we have bus, light rail service to the job centers. And then the other area is kind of within a mile of job centers. So you don't want to go further and further out. You don't want to say you want something affordable. You've got to go out, you know, 10 miles east of Keensburg and you can find something for 300. Fine. But you have an hour commute. You're on the road. It costs you all that money for gas and it leads to more traffic for everybody. So, you know, again, that's happening. We need to change that paradigm. So those more affordable housing options are closer to job centers. And there's multiple job centers across the Denver metro. It's not just downtown Denver. People think, oh, it's downtown Denver. I mean, there's jobs in Thornton. There's commercial jobs in Broomfield. There's commercial jobs, you know, in Denver Tech Center. I mean, it's kind of all these areas where we want to give people the opportunity to live close to their jobs.

background.text: And we need to do more as a society to support those who keep us safe, our law enforcement officers, our firefighters. You're absolutely right. background.speaker: SPEAKER_01
background.text: Do we have, I mean, Democrats in recent years have been blamed for reducing, you know, calling for things like defunding the police. Not to say that you called for that in any way. Or do you feel like they get the support in the community and are treated as the heroes that they are?

ground_truth: There's a lot of people that work in law enforcement, just like there's a lot of teachers your kids might have at school. There's a lot of firefighters.
